title: Security pen test & patching/SDLC review - Acme Bank
summary: Redwood and Acme Bank reviewed the recent pen test results and discussed remediation timelines, vulnerability management, patch cadence, and secure SDLC integration. Action items: Redwood to share annotated pen test report and SOC2 docs; Acme to confirm patch window and prioritize two medium findings. Agreed follow-up in two weeks for status and verification testing.
topics: Secure SDLC and code review automation
Encryption at rest and KMS key management
Data residency and private deployment options
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about 45 minutes. I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our SE.
[00:07] Marcus Holt: Yep thanks, I'm Marcus, CISO at Acme. We have Aisha and David on. We're primarily here to go over the pen test results you sent and talk about patch cadence and how Redwood integrates into our SDLC.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Great, thanks Marcus. Quick agenda: hit high-level findings, then dig into the mediums, talk remediation timelines, and then cover logs/KMS/SSO. Sound OK?
[00:29] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. We did a quick read of the report; some of the tooling flagged misconfig or outdated libs. Wanted to get your take on risk and how fast you can remediate.
[00:38] Priya Nair: Totally. I'll be upfront: a couple of findings were third-party library CVEs noted as medium. Redwood's hosted infra is containerized and we have a regular patch pipeline; for hosted customers we patch base images weekly but some app-layer deps are on a different cadence.
[00:50] David Nguyen: Can you define "weekly"—is that auto-rolled or requires customer approval? We have strict change windows.
[00:56] Jordan Lee: For patching infra we can do rolling patch windows that are configurable per-account. By default we have a weekly AMI rebuild and can schedule it in your maintenance window; any app-level dependency updates we coordinate with customers to avoid regressions.
[01:10] Marcus Holt: The report flagged an auth bypass scenario on one endpoint in the management plane labeled medium. Does that map to your public API or internal admin consoles?
[01:20] Priya Nair: That one maps to our internal admin console — not exposed on the public inference API. We reproduced it in lab; patch is in QA today, mitigation is a config hardening that we can backport.
[01:28] Aisha Khan: Good to hear it's not public. We still need timeline and verification steps.
[01:33] Priya Nair: We aim to push the fix to prod in 3 business days pending QA. We'll provide a verification checklist and can enable additional audit logging for that component for 30 days for you to validate.
[01:45] Marcus Holt: OK mark that as high priority. Next, the KMS handling — the pen test mentioned weak key rotation for a specific tenant flow. Clarify your KMS usage and rotation cadence.
[01:58] Jordan Lee: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS in Private deployments and KMS integrations in Dedicated; for hosted accounts we use a managed KMS with a 90-day rotation by default. We can provide a dedicated key for Acme under a BYOK flow if you prefer faster rotation and separation.
[02:14] David Nguyen: BYOK would be ideal. How do you integrate with HSMs and can we audit key access?
[02:20] Priya Nair: Yes, we support AWS CloudHSM and Azure Key Vault HSM-backed keys. Access is logged to our audit trail and we can forward key usage events to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch forwarding.
[02:30] Marcus Holt: We also need assurances around SOC2 / ISO; do you have the report and can you provide scope and last audit date?
[02:36] Jordan Lee: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II as of 2025-10, and ISO 27001 certified 2025-09. We'll share the latest attestations and the control matrix. I'll drop that in the shared folder with the pen test artifacts.
[02:49] Aisha Khan: Great. On RBAC and SSO — the report called out overly permissive service roles in one deployment. What's Redwood's recommended RBAC model and how granular can role scoping be?
[03:02] Priya Nair: We support SAML/SCIM provisioning for SSO and fine-grained RBAC by route and model. Roles can be scoped to project, model, and environment. We can also map groups to least-privileged roles during initial onboarding.
[03:13] David Nguyen: Do you record admin actions? We need immutable audit logs for changes to routing or model pinning.
[03:19] Priya Nair: Yes, admin actions are logged with timestamp, actor, and action. Logs are retained per your contract (default 90 days) and can be extended. We can also stream logs to your SIEM for long-term retention.
[03:29] Marcus Holt: On data residency — is customer data moved across regions for failover? Acme requires EU-only storage for certain datasets.
[03:36] Jordan Lee: We support region pinning; data residency is configurable and we can guarantee EU-only storage and processing for pinned models and data. Cross-region replication is opt-in and we would document that in the SLA.
[03:48] Aisha Khan: The pen test also highlighted some insecure temp file handling in a debug endpoint. It was low severity but reproducible. Is that something in the product roadmap?
[03:58] Priya Nair: That debug endpoint was legacy and slated for deprecation; we've already removed it from public images in the last patch. We'll confirm it's absent from your tenant and include the commit/link.
[04:08] Jordan Lee: Quick note on vulnerability management: Redwood has a triage board; severity mapping roughly follows CVSS. For medium findings we aim for fix within 7 business days for infra and 14 for app-level unless blocked by customer change windows. We escalate anything marked high immediately.
[04:21] David Nguyen: Who owns the triage? If we submit a finding, do we get a ticket and status updates?
[04:26] Priya Nair: Yes, you get a ticket in our security tracker; we'll include remediation plan, assignee, and ETA. We also support coordinated disclosure windows for non-prod exploits.
[04:36] Marcus Holt: For verification testing, do you support re-tests by third-party pen testers? Any need for special creds?
[04:44] Priya Nair: We welcome re-tests. We can provide a temporary test client and a scoped environment or schedule a read-only snapshot. We ask you to coordinate to avoid production impact.
[04:55] Aisha Khan: About secure SDLC — how do you prevent regressions? Are there automated SCA checks, dependency scanning, and PR gating?
[05:03] Jordan Lee: Yes — our CI pipeline runs SCA, dynamic scans on staging, and we gate merges on test coverage and vulnerability thresholds. We also run scheduled dependency updates and keep a changelog for customers.
[05:14] David Nguyen: What's the patching cadence again? If we want faster rollouts for critical issues, can we request an expedited window?
[05:20] Priya Nair: Yes, expedited patches for critical/high are supported with SLAs. We'll coordinate with your change board; for hosted customers we can do out-of-band patching for high-risk findings.
[05:31] Marcus Holt: Ok recap: 1) Admin console auth bypass — Redwood to patch in 3 business days and provide verification logs. 2) KMS BYOK option — Redwood to share integration docs and implementation plan. 3) Debug endpoint removed — confirm commit. 4) Share SOC2/ISO attestations and control matrix. 5) Provide annotated pen test report with remediation notes.
[05:51] Jordan Lee: Yep that's our understanding. Anything else?
[05:55] Aisha Khan: Can you also give us recommended configuration for audit log retention and SIEM forwarding? We have compliance asking for 12 months retention.
[06:04] Priya Nair: Default is 90 days but we can extend to 12 months as an add-on. We'll include a spreadsheet of retention options and estimated cost.
[06:14] Marcus Holt: Great. We'll want an internal verification checklist and then schedule a verification call in two weeks.
[06:20] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. We'll send the artifacts and propose a follow-up time. Thanks everyone.
[06:26] (end)
